goals: Quantify water partitioning (ET, surface runoff, subsurface drainage/recharge) across elevation and soil gradients
Validate simulated water table depth against USGS wells and snow water equivalent against SNOTEL stations
key_processes: Water table dynamics and soil moisture storage

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM can resolve elevation-driven precipitation/snow gradients (via NLDAS-2 12 km forcing) and soil texture controls on infiltration/recharge. Stratified spatial sampling spans the domain's heterogeneity. Validation pinned to available observations (wells, SNOTEL).

answerable: Elevation control on partitioning via precipitation gradients and snow vs rain (NLDAS-2 resolves ~15 distinct precip values across 1625 m relief)
Soil texture control on infiltration and recharge (SSURGO per-column)
Water table depth validation against USGS wells (co-located)
SWE validation against SNOTEL (co-located, with 12 km averaging caveat)
Per-column partitioning fluxes (ET, surface runoff, subsurface drainage QDRAI)

not_answerable.why: ELM columns are independent 1-D (no lateral transport or routing). Cannot natively produce watershed-aggregated streamflow for gage comparison.
not_answerable.needs: Runoff routing/aggregation tool to sum column surface runoff and baseflow (QDRAI) to gage locations

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified by elevation and soil texture, with validation columns pinned to observation locations

bands: mid (900-1500 m): rain-snow transition, maximum recharge sensitivity

classes: coarse (sandy loam, high conductivity): valley alluvium
fine (loam/clay loam, lower conductivity): hillslopes and uplands

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 elevation bands × 2 soil classes = 6 strata. Sample 1-2 columns per stratum (light replication in rain-snow transition where sensitivity is highest) = 9 exploratory columns. This is the minimum to span the drivers while honoring 'a handful of representative columns'.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns at valley bottoms (where recharge accumulates and wells are located), the rain-snow transition zone (900-1500 m, maximum climate sensitivity), and high ridges (snow-dominated endmember). Avoid uniform grid; oversample the transition zone.
sampling_strategy.replication: Light replication (2 columns) in the mid-elevation rain-snow transition stratum to capture variability in the most sensitive zone.

sampling_plan.reason: Rain-dominated, high infiltration capacity, valley recharge accumulation zone
Rain-dominated, lower infiltration, tests soil texture control at low elevation
Rain-snow transition (maximum sensitivity), high conductivity, strong snowmelt recharge signal — replicated
Rain-snow transition, lower conductivity, tests soil control on snowmelt partitioning — replicated
Snow-dominated, thin/coarse alpine soils, minimal recharge endmember
Snow-dominated, finer upland soils, tests high-elevation soil control — includes SNOTEL co-location

validation_design.comparison: co-located: place validation columns at well coordinates, compare simulated ZWT to observed WTD time series
validation_design.n_validation_points: 3-5 (depends on well density and data quality in domain)

validation_design.comparison: co-located: place validation columns at SNOTEL coordinates, compare simulated H2OSNO to observed peak SWE and melt timing. Caveat: 12 km NLDAS cells average over terrain, expect underestimation at high-elevation ridgetop stations.
validation_design.metric: peak SWE bias, melt date difference, seasonal RMSE

validation_design.comparison: aggregated: requires summing column surface runoff (QOVER) and baseflow proxy (QDRAI) across the upstream contributing area, then routing to gage. NOT co-located (1-D columns have no native routing).
validation_design.metric: monthly flow bias, annual water balance closure, hydrograph correlation
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on gage locations and ability to delineate contributing areas

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (1980-2018, full period for climatology), native SSURGO soil per column, WTD-informed warm start from Fan 2013 equilibrium (preferred over multi-year spin-up)

requires_capabilities.why: Question targets recharge, a slow equilibrium process. Cold-start artifacts (uniform 8.8 m WTD, zero recharge during fill) would dominate. Fan-based initialization sets realistic per-column water table and aquifer storage.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Meaningful recharge and water table validation without multi-year spin-up cost

requires_capabilities.why: ELM columns are independent 1-D. To validate against USGS streamflow gauges, need to sum column surface runoff (QOVER) and subsurface drainage (QDRAI) over the upstream contributing area and route to gage location.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Integrated streamflow validation (partial answer: can still validate partitioning fluxes per-column and WTD/SWE co-located)

requires_capabilities.why: Sampling strategy specifies elevation bands and placement logic (valley bottoms, rain-snow transition, ridges). Downstream expander needs DEM to select actual coordinates matching these rules.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Deterministic translation of strategy to concrete column locations

requires_capabilities.capability: Gridded soil texture data (SSURGO) for stratification
requires_capabilities.why: Sampling strategy stratifies by soil texture (coarse vs fine). Expander needs gridded soil data to identify dominant classes and place columns accordingly.

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS well and SNOTEL station coordinate/metadata ingest
requires_capabilities.why: Validation design pins columns to observation locations. Need station coordinates and metadata (elevation, period of record) to place validation columns and match time periods.

requires_capabilities.capability: HUC boundary resolver for domain clipping
requires_capabilities.why: Domain is HUC 17030002. Need to clip DEM, soil, and observation locations to the watershed boundary.
requires_capabilities.blocks: Ensuring all columns and observations are in-domain

assumptions: NLDAS-2 12 km forcing adequately resolves the elevation-precipitation gradient across 1625 m relief (guidance confirms ~15 distinct precip values for this relief)
SNOTEL stations at high elevations will show underestimated SWE due to 12 km cell averaging over terrain (expected, not a failure)
Fan 2013 equilibrium WTD is an acceptable initial condition proxy for the Naches watershed (some drift expected as ELM's 1-D equilibrium differs from Fan's lateral-flow equilibrium)
Dominant soil classes can be identified from SSURGO and mapped to coarse vs fine texture stratification
USGS wells have sufficient temporal coverage (multi-year records) to validate simulated water table dynamics
The user accepts that streamflow validation requires a post-processing aggregation step (not native to the 1-D column framework)
open_questions: What is the period of record for the USGS wells? Do they span multiple years for seasonal/interannual validation?
Are the SNOTEL stations distributed across the elevation gradient, or clustered at high elevations?
Does the user want a specific forcing period (e.g. recent decade, drought vs wet years), or the full 1980-2018 climatology?
Is there a specific USGS gage of interest for streamflow validation, or should we target the watershed outlet?
Should we include a sensitivity test on soil hydraulic parameters (e.g. saturated conductivity) to quantify uncertainty in the recharge estimates?
